§4.5 Heading Depth Across Pages

📚 Document rule — needs other pages of the document; decided once and applied on every page

headings-heading-depth-across-pages · headings rule layout

✅ Normative

A new page MUST NOT restart the heading hierarchy. A heading MUST be given the depth its place in the document implies, and a top-level heading MUST appear only where the page prints one.

A page break is a printing accident, not a structural boundary. The section that was open at the foot of one page is still open at the head of the next, and a heading that continues it keeps its depth.

page 4 …    ## 9.2 Pressure
                9.2.1 Pascal's Law          ← depth 3: inside 9.2
─── page break ───
page 5 …    9.2.2 Variation with Depth      ← still depth 3, not a fresh top level

Depth comes from the document, not the page

Two signals settle almost every case, in this order:

  1. Printed numbering. 9.2.1 sits under 9.2 sits under 9. Where the document numbers its sections, the numbering MUST decide the depth, even where the typography disagrees.
  2. Typography, compared across pages. Where nothing is numbered, a heading's depth MUST be judged against the other headings of the same document, not against the rest of its own page. The largest line on page 5 is not automatically a top-level heading.

A subsection MUST NOT come out at the same depth as its parent, or shallower. If 9.2 is depth 2 then 9.2.1 is depth 3, on whatever page it lands.

Decks are the exception

In a slide deck the slides are peers and each slide title is legitimately top level. Whether the document is a deck is decided once for the whole document — see Document Type§4.4 — never slide by slide.

A single page

Where only one page is available, the hierarchy the page itself shows MUST be consistent — a subsection always deeper than its parent — and the depth MUST be taken from printed numbering where there is any. Where the absolute depth depends on pages that are not available, the output takes the depth the page supports and asserts nothing more.

Whether it is a heading at all

Recognising Ambiguous Headings§6.7 separates standalone section titles from run-in labels, repeated item labels and captions. Principal statement and numbered schedule titles are structural; a company line directly above one stays a separate paragraph (see Stacked Headings§6.9), as do units lines. A title inside a grid is transcribed once, in its table position.

The following MUST NOT be rendered as headings:

  • a running header — see Recurring Page Furniture§4.6;
  • a label naming the kind of document, such as ORIGINAL ARTICLE or EXHIBIT 2 — it is text; the title beneath it is the heading;
  • a value typed into a form field, however prominent;
  • a table or figure caption — see Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3.

Related

  • Block Classes§5.3 — Title vs Section-header
  • Recurring Page Furniture§4.6 — a running header never earns a depth at all
  • Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3 — a caption never becomes a heading
